title: Usage Breakdown Normalization Pipeline for Per-Route/Model/Customer Billing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The Console needs a single, deterministic service that turns raw telemetry (request traces, token counts, model variant info, batching metadata, and KV/cache hits) into normalized per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency attributions that power dashboards, chargeback reports, and SLA alerts. Current upstream pipelines emit heterogeneous rows (different schemas across model adapters and runtimes) and attribute shared compute (batching and KV cache amortization) inconsistently, producing noisy customer-facing numbers and hard-to-reconcile invoices.

Scope: Build a normalization and apportionment pipeline (stateless compute layer + durable aggregation layer) that: 1) canonicalizes telemetry events into a stable intermediate schema, 2) applies well-documented cost-splitting primitives (prefix amortization, batch crediting, kv-cache amortization), 3) produces time-windowed rollups per route/model/customer suitable for the Console and billing exports, and 4) exposes explainability metadata for every attribution row (why a given token got charged to X).

Non-goals: This ticket does not modify billing contracts or replace the existing billing ledger. It also does not redesign frontend dashboards; it provides the corrected inputs for them. It does not cover embedding-cost allocation for offline vectorization jobs (separate project).

Key concepts introduced: 
- Telemetry fingerprinting: deterministic key for grouping related RPCs that share compute (e.g., continuous-batch window id).
- Amortization credits: first-class tokens assigned to requests that share a batch or KV cache warmup, used to split fixed GPU setup cost across members.
- Normalized schema (NB: stable field names): event_id, fingerprint, route_id, model_id, model_variant, customer_id, token_in, token_out, latency_ms, batch_size, kv_hit, host_cost_usd, timestamp, explain_links.

High-level flow: 
1) Ingest component-level telemetry from existing producers (ingress logs, model-runtime trace emitter, batching service) via Kafka with a light validation layer.
2) Apply canonicalizer transforms (map field names, normalize model variant aliases, enrich with route metadata from Console cache).
3) Group by fingerprint and compute amortization credits for batch and KV cache events.
4) Emit attributed rows to a long-window aggregator (ClickHouse/BigQuery) for rollups and to an explainability store (search index or small timeseries DB) for per-event inspection.
5) Downstream rollups compute per-route/model/customer cost & p50/p95 latency slices and write to the Console API cache for immediate UI consumption.

Operational constraints: near-real-time (1–5 minute freshness for dashboards, hourly for invoicing), idempotent ingest, tolerant to dropped telemetry (have heuristics for conservative attribution), and resource-efficient to avoid ballooning storage costs.

Success metrics: 
- Reduce unexplained reconciliation variance between Console and billing system to <1.5% for top-100 customers.
- Dashboard freshness SLA: 95% of route rollups updated within 5 minutes.
- Explainability coverage: 99% of attributed cost rows include an explain_link referencing the originating fingerprint and contributing events.

Stakeholders: Console backend (product), Billing team, Platform Observability, Runtime Eng, Solutions/SE for customer-facing reconciliation support.
acceptance_criteria: A canonicalizer job that transforms heterogeneous telemetry messages into the normalized schema and emits validation failures to a dead-letter topic
Batch and KV cache amortization algorithm implemented as a library with unit tests and documented formulas
Aggregated rollups (1m and 1h windows) available in analytics store with the per-route/model/customer primary keys
Per-attribute explainability link stored and resolvable to the set of contributing event_ids
Integration test that replays a representative day of telemetry and reproduces expected top-customer cost splits within 2% of golden dataset
Dashboard endpoints return rollup data within 5 minutes of event time for 95% of routes during a synthetic load test
